name: Devtools.
line: A panel in the page, run as an isolate of its own, showing the isolates, the bus, the kernel’s own events and a live record log.
text: Devtools are experimental. `connectDevtools(kernel)` from `@isoloop/devtools` (new in 0.1.0-next.4; the log and its skipped count from 0.1.0-next.5; the health ring, the Events tab and the Messages name from 0.1.0-next.8) puts a button in a corner of the page, ringed by twelve arcs that show the kernel’s health, each arc a stretch of isolates coloured by their worst state. `healthStatus` picks the ring, a variant that also fills the logo, or a plain white ring.

A click or Alt+Shift+D opens a panel with four tabs. Isolates: each one’s state, lag, busy time, crash restarts, pool and memory, with Restart, Kill and Block on each row, and the pools on a tab of their own. Bus: each topic’s rate, head offset and retained count, each subscription’s lag and credit, and rejected publishes. Events: the kernel’s own history, isolates changing state, crashing or failing and the bus restarting, up to 6,000 events for this page session and for each of the last three sessions before it, so a crash that ended in a reload can be read back. Messages: live records, at most 50 a second, with a count of what that cap left out; a row opens into its value and its record.

The panel is a visual isolate in its own worker, never pooled, so a crash or hang in it doesn’t reach the page, and the supervisor restarts it like any other. It lists itself, marked devtools. It reads the kernel’s inspection feed, `kernel.inspect()`, through the `inspect` grant on a port of its own, so it keeps working while the bus restarts, and its traffic stays out of the bus figures it shows. The dev MCP reads the same feed for a coding agent.

Memory per isolate is measured only in Chromium on a cross-origin isolated page, while a reader listens, so a figure can be many seconds old. Nothing gates the controls in production, and killing a pool member stops its whole worker. With nothing reading it, the feed costs a buffer of the last 200 events, about 18 KB on the plant dashboard; what an open feed costs is on the plant example’s measurements.

proof.test: restarts after a crash, like any isolate
mounts its button in the corner and opens a panel that lists itself
keeps logging through a bus restart
counts the records left out over the cap, from zero each time it opens
keeps the last 200 events, oldest first, whether inspected or not
has a second level of tabs: pools under Isolates, topics, subscriptions and rejected under Bus
lists the kernel events, newest first, and opens one to its data
'radar' also fills the logo with the twelve colours
stores them, and a later session can read them back
keeps only the last few sessions
